original.target_description: Study 1, preregistered US cross-sectional survey: in-person social portfolio diversity predicting composite global well-being, controlling for amount of social interaction. Printed focal regression on p. 2.

n.sample_role: Participants; printed model-specific n, disputed by the replication authors.
n.exclusions: Original text does not establish exclusions for this model. Replication report pp. 6–8 disputes this printed n and reports reproducing the original calculation with N = 500; not substituted for the original printed value.

replication.target_description: Replication of Study 1: linear regression of composite well-being on social portfolio diversity controlling for proportion of episodes involving in-person interaction. Social portfolio diversity set to 0 for participants reporting no in-person interactions; first focal replication result on p. 4.

n.sample_role: Participants in focal regression after exclusions; zero-interaction participants retained with diversity set to 0.
n.exclusions: 971 completed; 6 failed attention check and 4 excluded for data quality; 961 analyzed.
n.location: p. 4, Summary of Study and Results, exclusions and focal replication regression
n.quote:
We excluded 6 participants who
    failed the attention check from the data analysis, and 4 due to data quality issues, leaving N = 961.

es.location: p. 4, Summary of Study and Results, zero-interaction participants retained

p.location: p. 4, Summary of Study and Results, zero-interaction participants retained

reported_success.location: p. 1, Executive Summary; p. 4, Summary of Study and Results
reported_success.quote: Although this finding replicated, this paper has serious weaknesses in transparency and clarity.

notes: Title verified for original and OSF primary replication PDF; supplied replication reference is only WITHDRAWN, while the publicly accessible primary report is Report #5 by Amanda Metskas, June 29, 2023. Original source is the frozen Europe PMC full-text parse; page 2 verified against the published PDF at the institutional repository. Original n is retained as explicitly printed for the focal model but marked uncertain because replication authors dispute its accuracy. Replication p. 4 also prints a separate analysis excluding 116 zero-interaction participants (β = 0.097, P = 0.012, n = 845); it is not merged with the selected n = 961 analysis. Replication authors state that using the control variable as actually calculated in the original rather than as described produces nonsignificant replication results; they conclude replication based on their preregistered described calculation. Replication p. 9 table prints an inconsistent upper CI limit 0.725 versus p. 4 0.735 for the selected model; no conversion or CI extraction performed.
